answer: Each task is derived from a domain-separated hash of its identifier and a specified future drand quicknet pulse; labels such as quartz, river, and shale separate task classes but add no secret entropy. Because the threshold-BLS pulse is unpredictable before publication and publicly verifiable afterward, agents cannot precompute valid answers offline. Commit-reveal deadlines and per-identity resource limits make mass Sybil attempts costly rather than letting beacon randomness alone prove uniqueness.
